candidate_relations.label: Sickle Cell Retinopathy, proliferative
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly states no peripheral neovascularization is present, ruling out proliferative retinopathy. The findings—ischemic macular whitening, hyperreflective INL/OPL plaques on OCT, abnormal macular capillary bed on FA, and middle retinal layer atrophy—are hallmarks of PAMM, not proliferative sickle cell retinopathy. While both share the sickle cell etiology, the subtype and anatomical scope are incompatible.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Proliferative sickle cell retinopathy implies peripheral neovascularization (sea-fan lesions), which is explicitly absent here; the reference diagnosis is paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) in the context of sickle cell disease, a distinct macular ischemic entity

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis specifies PAMM as a distinct macular ischemic syndrome within sickle cell disease; proliferative subtype is explicitly excluded by clinical findings
